verdict.summary: Amkor is a strategically important but low-margin beneficiary of advanced packaging, not a software-like AI compounder. Q2 2026 net sales reached a record $1.898 billion, up 26% year over year; GAAP gross margin improved to 16.8% from 12.0%, operating margin to 10.5% from 6.1%, and diluted EPS to $0.70 from $0.22. The AI transmission is concrete: high-performance compute requires more complex assembly, test and packaging, and Amkor's partnerships with TSMC and NVIDIA position it to capture outsourced work as U.S. capacity expands. The constraint is capital intensity. Management guided $2.5-$3.0 billion of 2026 capex, roughly one-third to two-fifths of trailing revenue, while Q3 revenue guidance of $1.95-$2.05 billion demands continued utilization gains to protect thin margins. At 9.7x EV/EBITDA the valuation is far less demanding than most AI hardware names, but the chart remains below all three displayed EMAs. The 65/100 grade is defensible; the watch state still requires $51.49 confirmation.

business.overview:
Amkor provides outsourced semiconductor assembly and test services, converting fabricated wafers into qualified packages for communications, automotive, consumer and computing customers. Revenue follows unit demand, package complexity, utilization and product mix; unlike chip designers, Amkor absorbs substantial factory and equipment costs.

AI reaches Amkor through advanced packaging and test for high-performance processors, memory and chiplet systems. Higher I/O density, thermal constraints and multi-die integration increase packaging content per device, while the TSMC Arizona collaboration and NVIDIA partnership can channel U.S. AI/HPC programs into Amkor's planned capacity.

The model breaks when customers delay ramps, internalize packaging, or leave new plants underutilized. Thin gross margins magnify pricing, yield, earthquake, currency and mix shocks, and the $2.5-$3.0B 2026 capex program must earn acceptable returns rather than merely add strategic capacity. Customer prepayments help fund the Arizona advanced-packaging build, but they also evidence concentration and contractual performance obligations. The model breaks if utilization lags planned capacity, mobile demand softens, or leading customers internalize packaging rather than outsourcing it.
business.moat: Amkor's moat is manufacturing qualification at scale: advanced package process know-how, test capability, customer certifications and a global factory footprint that is difficult to replicate quickly. The TSMC and NVIDIA relationships can improve program access, but the moat earns only low-to-mid-teens gross margins unless advanced-package mix and utilization rise.

filings.finding: The Q2 2026 Form 10-Q supports the $1.898B revenue base, 16.8% GAAP gross margin, approximately balanced cash and debt position and capital-intensive manufacturing risks that govern free-cash-flow quality.
The July 27 earnings Form 8-K and Exhibit 99.1 support $1.898B revenue, $0.70 GAAP diluted EPS, Q3 revenue guidance of $1.95B-$2.05B and FY2026 capex guidance of $2.5B-$3.0B.
The FY2025 Form 10-K supplies the OSAT customer, utilization, geographic, earthquake, pricing and manufacturing-risk baseline; it does not establish an ATM or a new issuer common-stock sale.

The final February 13 Form 424B7 prices a Kim-family secondary of 10.0M shares plus a 1.5M-share underwriter option at $48.75, or $487.5M gross before the option. Amkor receives no proceeds; the preliminary accession 0001193125-26-048716 is the same chain and is not counted again.

The May 5 Form 8-K records completed issuance of $1.15B of 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2031, including the fully exercised $150M option. Initial conversion is 9.4013 shares per $1,000 principal and the maximum rate exposes up to 16,487,435 common shares. This is convertible debt, not an ATM or completed common offering; capped calls reduce economic dilution but do not cancel the security-level claim.

Geographic manufacturing exposure creates earthquake, currency, trade and supply-chain risk.
